summary: Lolo NF L-4 tower on Cube Iron Mountain, in 1935 and 1936 newspaper items; sources disagree on destroyed in 1959 versus removed; now gone.

facts.status_note: Sources disagree on how it ended: firelookout.com says destroyed in 1959; the Forest Lookouts page says removed, with no date.

access.note: A hiking guide describes a trail route up to the summit; the sources read describe no closure.

visit.trail_note: Hiking guide: 8.5 miles round trip on Trails 459 and 450, with a side trail up to the summit.

events.note: firelookout.com gives 1935 for the L-4 tower; a June 1935 newspaper item says Cube Iron Peak took the place of Mount Headley as a lookout station.
An August 1936 newspaper item names Halvor Ekern as the lookout on Cube Iron.
firelookout.com says destroyed in 1959. The Forest Lookouts page says removed, with no date.

evidence.supports: Sanders County; tower listed as gone
evidence.quote: Sanders Cube Iron Mountain 47.68700 -115.29112 Tower Gone

evidence.supports: June 1935: Cube Iron Peak took the place of Headley
evidence.quote: Cube Iron Peak takes the place of Headley.

evidence.supports: peaks in the Cabinet dropped as lookout stations because of visual mapping
evidence.quote: Mount Headley is among some of the peaks discontinued as lookout stations in the Cabinet due to the visual observation mapping on the forest.

evidence.supports: August 1936: Halvor Ekern as the lookout on Cube Iron
evidence.quote: Halvor Ekern, lookout on Cube Iron

evidence.supports: three people hiked up to visit Ekern in 1936
evidence.quote: Mrs. Ekern, Carol and Delores Helman hiked up to Cube Iron to visit with Halvor Monday

evidence.supports: trail route to the summit on Trails 459 and 450
Trail 450 is part of the route
side trail up to the summit
evidence.quote: Take the side trail to the right (west) up to the summit of Cube Iron Mountain.
On top you can see the American Selkirks to the west, and the Cabinet Mountain Wilderness to the east.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says destroyed in 1959; the Forest Lookouts page says removed, with no date. Both are reported in the story; the record status gone fits both.

sources.title: Cube Iron Mtn. Fire Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: The 1935 and 1936 items are newspaper quotes printed on the Forest Lookouts page; the original Sanders County Independent-Ledger was not opened. The destroyed-versus-removed conflict is unresolved. The access and trail details come from an undated hiking guide and are used for access only; no source describes the lookout site itself today. The guide gives the summit as 7,110 ft; the record elevation_m is still null, so it could be filled with a note on the source. Possible next step: 1959 Sanders County newspapers for the end of the tower.
